nodes.title: Note: MiniMax H3
widgets_values:
## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task using the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. It takes any mix of reference images, videos, and standalone audio, and weaves them into the generation to lock in a character's identity, a style, a motion, a camera move, or a voice.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images / ref_videos / ref_video_audios / ref_audios**: up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos (each may carry its own paired soundtrack), and 3 standalone reference audio clips
- **prompt**: reference the inputs by tag, in the exact order they were connected, for example `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`, then describe the target scene, motion, and audio
- **ref_image_size**: `match` scales references down to the generation's resolution (faster); `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity, at the cost of speed since reference tokens ride along every sampling step
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector.
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node

**Sampling and decode**

- Sampler: `res_multistep`. `beta` or `normal` scheduler tends to outperform `simple` for reference-heavy prompts like this one
- The sampler's joint audio+video `LATENT` output feeds directly into both `VAEDecode` (video, `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16`) and `VAEDecodeAudio` (audio, `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32`); each decode node automatically pulls its own half out of the packed latent. `CreateVideo` then muxes the two into a single MP4 with synced sound
- The diffusion model here is `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`, a different set of weights from the `fl2va` model used by the t2v/i2v templates

Ref2va's output is very sensitive to prompt wording; matching the reference tags precisely and being explicit about which reference drives which part of the shot tends to work best.

nodes.title: Prompt
widgets_values:
Create a photorealistic 10-second horizontal 16:9 talking-to-camera vlog video with an f/16 aperture look and deep depth of field.

@[Image 1] is the sole character identity reference. Preserve her exact facial identity, hairstyle, outfit with long sleeves, body proportions and appearance throughout the entire video.

The girl is seated behind her desk in a home workspace.

Use one continuous take from directly in front of her, approximately at her seated eye level. The slightly wide-angle landscape composition shows her face, shoulders and upper body, with a small portion of the desk along the bottom edge. Keep the view of her unobstructed, with her face and the background in focus.

0–2 seconds — INTRO

Already seated, she briefly reaches forward, just beyond the frame, to make a small framing adjustment. The view shifts slightly, centers on her and settles into a stationary composition.

She brings her hand back, looks into the lens and says with an impressed smile and slightly raised eyebrows:

“This method is incredible!”

2–7 seconds — DEMONSTRATION AND SUNLIGHT REACTION

She leans closer while keeping her entire face inside the frame.

As she speaks, she places her right index finger against her cheek, gives it one small, gentle sideways pull, then immediately releases it and lowers her hand to the desk. This is a single gesture performed only once.

She says conversationally, looking directly into the lens:

“Look at my skin—it’s so real. No plastic skin at all.”

Around the middle of this explanation, direct sunlight suddenly shines through the window onto her face. She instinctively squints and tilts her head slightly in reaction, with a small amused smile, while continuing her sentence without stopping. The sunlight remains for the rest of the shot.

7–10 seconds — OUTRO

Her expression shifts into amused disbelief. Her eyebrows rise, and she briefly lifts one hand in a small palm-up gesture beside her shoulder.

With a soft, breathy exhale of amazement, she says:

“Pff… this can’t be real!”

She finishes with an incredulous smile and a tiny head shake, beginning to ease back into her seat. End with natural movement.

DIALOGUE AND AUDIO

Speak only the quoted dialogue, once each, in the order shown. Accurate lip-sync, clear articulation and a natural conversational pace that fits the 10-second duration.

Low female voice with a casual creator tone. Clear, close speech with quiet indoor ambience and subtle clothing movement. No music.

CAMERA AND CONTINUITY

Horizontal 16:9 framing throughout, viewed directly from the front at her seated eye level.

One small framing adjustment at the beginning, followed by a stationary shot. The close-up comes entirely from her leaning forward.

Keep her whole face visible and her finger away from her mouth. Maintain consistent identity and continuous, anatomically correct movement.

No zoom, pans, orbiting, cuts, repeated cheek gestures, extra fingers, duplicated limbs, subtitles or on-screen text.
